title: Package Entry Points and the exports Field knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Package Entry Points and the exports Field?
options: Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Choose CommonJS or ECMAScript modules explicitly and keep public exports small and documented.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Choose CommonJS or ECMAScript modules explicitly and keep public exports small and documented.
questions.explanation: Choose CommonJS or ECMAScript modules explicitly and keep public exports small and documented. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Package Entry Points and the exports Field?
questions.explanation: “The main field” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Package Entry Points and the exports Field implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
